title: Ampleness lifts along a first order thickening of Noetherian schemes
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of Noetherian schemes (schemes [def-pc-scheme] that are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]) whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] has square zero, $\mathcal I^2=0$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and $j^*\mathcal L$ its pullback to $Z$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. If $j^*\mathcal L$ is ample on $Z$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], then $\mathcal L$ is ample on $X$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS (coherent-lemma-ample-on-reduction, coherent.tex line 4737), proof, second and third paragraphs (the case $\mathcal I^2=0$): the exact sequence $0\to\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\to\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\to i_*i^*\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\to0$, Morphisms 01QY, the boundary derivation Cohomology 0B8S, Lemma 01XR (via 09MR) and Lemma 01YQ

proof.text: Write M_n=I tensor L^{tensor n}. The closed immersion's ideal sequence is 0 \to I \to O_X \to j_*O_Z \to 0. Since L^{tensor n} is locally free of rank one, tensoring is exact: I tensor L^{tensor n} \to L^{tensor n} is injective with image I L^{tensor n}. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-unit-quotient] with F=L^{tensor n}: L^{tensor n}/I L^{tensor n} is isomorphic to j_*j^*L^{tensor n}. Thus 0 \to M_n \to L^{tensor n} \to j_*j^*L^{tensor n} \to 0 is exact. The closed-immersion ideal I is quasi-coherent [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and M_n is quasi-coherent locally because L^{tensor n} is free of rank one. For every local a in I and v in M_n, av=0 since I^2=0 [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-annihilated] (2) with F=M_n: G_n:=j^*M_n is quasi-coherent on Z and j_*G_n is isomorphic to M_n. Since a closed immersion is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] for j and G_n gives H^1(X,M_n) = H^1(X,j_*G_n) isomorphic to H^1(Z,G_n) as O_X(X)-modules.

source.place: Cohomology Lemma 09MS, square-zero proof, exact sequence (equation-ses) and paragraph identifying I as an O_Z-module

proof.text: Fix x in X. As I^2=0, i.e. I(U)^2=0 on every affine open U [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], the quasi-coherent ideal I [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is contained in every prime of each affine coordinate ring; [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine] identifies j(Z)=V(I)=X, so x has a preimage z in Z. Ampleness of j^*L [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] supplies n>=1 and s in Gamma(Z,j^*L^{tensor n}) with z in the affine principal open Z_s. In the degree-n exact sequence of step 1, the obstruction to lifting s is its connecting class xi=partial(s) in H^1(X,M_n), identified with a class in H^1(Z,G_n) by the edge isomorphism of step 1.

source.place: Cohomology Lemma 09MS, square-zero proof, paragraph beginning 'Let x in X'

proof.text: Set O'=direct sum over m>=0 of L^{tensor m} and O=direct sum over m>=0 of j_*j^*L^{tensor m}, with multiplication by tensor product. These are sheaves of commutative O_X-algebras: locally a frame for the invertible L identifies O' with a polynomial algebra in one generator, so its multiplication is commutative; the quotient O is commutative too. The degreewise surjection from step 1 gives O' \to O with kernel K=direct sum over m>=0 of I tensor L^{tensor m}; products of two kernel terms land in I^2 tensor L^{tensor (a+b)}=0. Apply [lem-sc-boundary-derivation-square-zero] to O' \to O. By naturality of the long exact sequence for inclusion of a degree-m summand and projection onto it, projecting the boundary of the summed sequence to degree m is the boundary of the degree-m exact sequence. Thus the image of s in the degree-n summand has boundary xi. Induct on k>=1: for k=1 this is xi; if partial(s^k)=k s^{k-1}xi, the Leibniz rule gives partial(s^{k+1})=s partial(s^k)+s^k partial(s)=(k+1)s^k xi. Taking k=e+1 gives partial(s^{e+1})=(e+1)s^e xi, where s^e acts through O on K.

Apply [lem-sc-section-affine-open-kills-cohomology] on Z to the invertible module j^*L^{tensor n} [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible], its section s, the quasi-coherent module F=G_n from step 1, p=1, and the class xi transported through the edge isomorphism of step 1. Z is quasi-compact since it is Noetherian, and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; Z_s is affine by step 2. The node gives e>=0 for which multiplication by s^e kills xi in H^1(Z,G_n tensor (j^*L^{tensor n})^{tensor e}). This multiplication is induced by G_n \to G_n tensor (j^*L^{tensor n})^{tensor e}, f \mapsto f tensor s^e. Naturality of the affine-morphism edge isomorphism for this map identifies it with the action s^e xi in step 3. Thus partial(s^{e+1})=(e+1)s^e xi=0, and exactness of the degree-(e+1)n sequence lifts s^{e+1} to s' in Gamma(X,L^{tensor (e+1)n}).

By the stalkwise definition of X_{s'} in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], j^*s'=s^{e+1}, and a power has the same nonvanishing locus, so j^{-1}(X_{s'})=Z_s. The base change Z_s \to X_{s'} of j is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b), hence finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Since I^2=0, i.e. I(U)^2=0 on every affine open U [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], the quasi-coherent ideal I [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] lies in every prime of each affine coordinate ring; [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine] identifies j(Z)=V(I)=X, so the restricted map Z_s \to X_{s'} is surjective. Its source Z_s is affine by step 2. The target X_{s'} is Noetherian in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]: it is locally Noetherian as an open subscheme of X, and quasi-compact because any open subset of the Noetherian topological space X is quasi-compact. These four inputs to [lem-weil-pbc-finite-surjective-affine-target-noetherian] show X_{s'} is affine.

source.place: Cohomology Lemma 09MS, final paragraph, invocation of Lemma 01YQ

proof.text: X is quasi-compact by the Noetherian hypothesis, giving clause (1) of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. For every x in X, steps 2-5 produce s' in Gamma(X,L^{tensor (e+1)n}) with x in X_{s'} and X_{s'} affine. Here n>=1 from step 2 and e>=0 from step 4, so (e+1)n>=1. This is clause (2) of the ampleness definition, hence L is ample.
